content.title: About
content.content: Coconut flour is a dry product made from the dried meat of the coconut after the coconut oil has been pressed out. It has a delicate coconut aroma, a slightly sweet taste, and a very porous texture, making it an excellent gluten‑free flour substitute.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Coconut flour contains about 60 % dietary fiber, making it one of the most fibrous flours.
It is virtually gluten‑free and suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
Because of the high fat content in coconut meat, the flour has a low glycemic index.
Coconut flour is widely used in vegan baking for breads, cookies, and pancakes.
When baking with coconut flour you need more liquid, as it absorbs 3–4 times more moisture than wheat flour.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: The high amount of soluble and insoluble fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps stabilize blood sugar levels, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes or diabetes.

items.title: Contains medium‑chain triglycerides (MCT)
items.content: MCTs are quickly metabolized and can provide a fast source of energy.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for blood formation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Coconut flour contains phenolic compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Coconut allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coconut products, including flour.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Although most of the fat is MCT, it is still calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: A sudden increase in fiber intake can cause bloating or diarrhea.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Coconut flour may slow the absorption of certain drugs due to its fat‑binding properties.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coconut flour is used in gluten‑free baking: breads, muffins, cookies, pancakes, and as a coating. It pairs well with eggs, plant‑based milks, and other gluten‑free flours. Add it gradually and increase the liquid ratio in the recipe.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
